raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce on (#59478), the `fuse_allreduce_rms` pass now runs prefill all-reduce + add-RMSNorm as one FlyDSL kernel instead of falling back to HIP QuickReduce + RMSNorm. Stacked on #59478; only the last commit is new. Needs [ROCm/aiter#6369](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6369) (`QuickAllReduceInt4.allreduce_rmsnorm`), so this stays a draft until an AITER release ships it. #61020 builds on this PR to also fuse the MXFP4 activation quant.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for "FlyDSL QuickReduce RMSNorm", "quick reduce rmsnorm" and "flydsl allreduce". #56326 fuses AR + RMSNorm + per-token FP8 quant in the custom all-reduce kernel, and #55917 adds a plain FlyDSL all-reduce for RDNA4; neither touches the QuickReduce path.

## Claims

- FlyDSL QuickReduce and `fuse_allreduce_rms` can be on together. #59478's warning against combining them is removed.
- `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, MI355X, one run per arm: +4.4% geomean output throughput (+1.5% to +7.0% across 12 points), −7.2% mean TTFT and −4.1% mean TPOT, against #59478 with the fusion off as it recommends. The candidate arm also turns on AITER's existing decode-size fusion (see Limitations).
- The fused kernel is 1.06–1.12× faster than FlyDSL all-reduce + `rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_add` for 1k–16k tokens at hidden 8192 (ROCm/aiter#6369).
- Nothing changes unless `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_USE_FLYDSL=1`.

## Validation

**Unit tests.** CPU, with the ROCm platform selected; the deselected tests need GPUs.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/distributed/test_quick_all_reduce.py \
  -k "not test_custom_quick_allreduce and not graph"
```

```text
23 passed, 23 deselected in 3.95s
```

- `test_flydsl_int4_should_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_gates_operands`: the fused call is declined outside the QuickReduce window, for an unsupported hidden size, an fp32 weight, a non-contiguous residual and with FlyDSL off. Each of these would otherwise reach a kernel that cannot take the operands.
- `test_rocm_aiter_fused_rmsnorm_uses_flydsl_int4_for_prefill`: `_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` takes the FlyDSL path for a prefill-sized input, passes the kernel its operands (plain and Gemma norm), and never reaches HIP QuickReduce + RMSNorm.
- #59478's `test_rocm_aiter_fused_rmsnorm_uses_aiter_qr_rmsnorm_for_prefill[flydsl_qr]` now declines the FlyDSL kernel first, so it still checks the fallback to HIP QuickReduce + RMSNorm.

**Kernel evidence.** ROCm/aiter#6369 tests the fused kernel at TP 2, 4 and 8 on MI355X: within bf16 tolerance of the unfused FlyDSL path, bitwise equal across ranks, and the speedup above.

**End to end.** 8× MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` TP8, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7` with our Qwen3.8 MI355X performance PRs (including #57547 and #59478), this PR, and the AITER PR on AITER v0.1.24.post1. One run per arm on the same node, each server from empty vLLM, AITER and Triton caches.

- **Control:** #59478, `fuse_allreduce_rms: false`.
- **Candidate:** this PR, `fuse_allreduce_rms: true`.

Random dataset, `random-range-ratio 0.8`. Positive throughput deltas and negative TTFT/TPOT deltas favor this PR.

| ISL/OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Δ | Mean TTFT (ms) | Δ | Mean TPOT (ms) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k/1k | 4 | 320 → 334 | +4.5% | 456 → 394 | −13.6% | 11.8 → 11.3 | −3.9% |
| 8k/1k | 8 | 501 → 511 | +2.0% | 447 → 422 | −5.4% | 15.2 → 14.9 | −1.8% |
| 8k/1k | 16 | 718 → 734 | +2.2% | 663 → 614 | −7.3% | 21.1 → 20.7 | −2.0% |
| 8k/1k | 32 | 1008 → 1036 | +2.8% | 1383 → 1272 | −8.0% | 29.0 → 28.3 | −2.6% |
| 8k/1k | 64 | 1384 → 1429 | +3.3% | 2455 → 2289 | −6.8% | 42.5 → 41.2 | −3.0% |
| 8k/1k | 128 | 1738 → 1824 | +4.9% | 6051 → 5641 | −6.8% | 65.0 → 62.0 | −4.6% |
| 8k/1k | 256 | 2149 → 2271 | +5.7% | 11992 → 11033 | −8.0% | 103.1 → 97.8 | −5.2% |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 152 → 163 | +7.0% | 2794 → 2461 | −11.9% | 21.1 → 20.0 | −5.2% |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 216 → 229 | +5.9% | 5330 → 4969 | −6.8% | 63.4 → 60.0 | −5.3% |
| 60k/600 | 64 | 251 → 267 | +6.7% | 19968 → 18838 | −5.7% | 216.1 → 202.2 | −6.5% |
| 128k/1k | 4 | 128 → 130 | +1.5% | 5668 → 6299 | +11.1% \* | 24.8 → 23.6 | −4.6% |
| 128k/1k | 16 | 168 → 179 | +6.1% | 12830 → 10965 | −14.5% | 80.1 → 76.7 | −4.3% |
| **Geomean** | | | **+4.4%** | | **−7.2%** | | **−4.1%** |

\* 32 requests at concurrency 4 with 128k prompts, so mean TTFT depends heavily on how prefills queue behind each other. Every other point, including 128k at concurrency 16, has lower TTFT. The 8k concurrency-4 point is the first after server start and carries the largest TTFT delta; without it the TTFT geomean is −6.6%.

**Accuracy.** GPQA Diamond (thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, 100k max tokens), same servers, one run each:

| | GPQA Diamond |
|---|---|
| #59478, fusion off | 0.919 |
| this PR, `fuse_allreduce_rms: true` | 0.924 |

Per-question results were not kept for these runs, so this is an unpaired comparison; a paired rerun with flip counts and an exact McNemar p-value is pending.

**Reproduce:**

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_USE_FLYDSL=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=512 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"splitting_ops": [], "pass_config": {"fuse_allreduce_rms": true}}'
# control: "fuse_allreduce_rms": false

# one point; the rest are listed below the block
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 4 --request-rate inf

python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gpqa --num-threads 32 --max-tokens 100000 \
  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true, "think_end_token": "</think>"}'
```

<details>
<summary>All 12 points (seed, concurrency, prompts; warmup requests = concurrency)</summary>

| ISL/OSL | (seed, concurrency, prompts) |
|---|---|
| 8192/1024 | (1, 4, 32), (2, 8, 64), (3, 16, 96), (4, 32, 128), (5, 64, 256), (6, 128, 384), (7, 256, 768) |
| 60000/600 | (8, 4, 32), (9, 16, 96), (10, 64, 256) |
| 128000/1024 | (11, 4, 32), (12, 16, 96) |

</details>

The full runs also use the other PRs' options (`--gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_PREQUANTIZED_QKV=1`, MXFP4 targets for the shared experts and GDN projections, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING=1`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`); they are identical in both arms.

## Details

**Before.** The AITER all-reduce fusion pass sends fused all-reduces in the QuickReduce size range to AITER's HIP QuickReduce + RMSNorm. With FlyDSL QuickReduce on, turning the fusion on therefore gives up FlyDSL QuickReduce for exactly the prefill-sized all-reduces it is fastest on. #59478 warns about the combination and recommends the fusion off, which leaves the residual add and RMSNorm as separate launches after every prefill all-reduce.

**After.** The AITER PR adds an add-RMSNorm epilogue to the FlyDSL kernel. On the non-one-stage branch, `_rocm_aiter_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_impl` asks `QuickAllReduce` first:

- `should_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(inp, residual, weight)` accepts the call when FlyDSL QuickReduce owns the payload (the `should_quick_allreduce` window), the kernel supports the hidden size (`QuickAllReduceInt4.supports_rmsnorm`, owned by AITER), and the residual and weight are bf16, contiguous and 16-byte aligned. It reads only tensor metadata, so it adds no host-device synchronization.
- `fused_allreduce_rmsnorm(...)` runs the fused kernel and returns `(out, residual_out)`, with Gemma (`1 + weight`) norms supported.

Decode sizes, which the one-stage custom all-reduce owns, and everything FlyDSL declines keep their current path. The methods live on `QuickAllReduce` because it already owns the FlyDSL object (#59478). +46 / −12 non-test lines.

**Limitations and CI gaps**

- **Arms.** The candidate turns on `fuse_allreduce_rms`, which also enables AITER's existing one-stage custom-AR fusion for decode-sized all-reduces. The end-to-end delta therefore covers that fusion as well as this PR. A three-arm run on nightly + #59478 only (fusion off; fusion on with HIP QuickReduce + RMSNorm; this PR) is pending.
- **Prefill coverage on main.** The image carries #57547. Without it, the fusion pass's compile range stops at the custom all-reduce's 64 MiB limit (4096 tokens at hidden 8192 in bf16), so with `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, prefill chunks of 4097–8192 tokens stay unfused.
- **Coverage.** Measured on gfx950, TP8, one model. The AITER kernel admits gfx942 but was tested only on gfx950. TP2/TP4, a second model, GSM8K and NIAH are pending.
- **CI.** The unit tests run in the MI355 "Distributed Features" step. The end-to-end runs need 8× MI355X and the 2.4T checkpoint, so they ran outside CI.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

</details>

detail.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse add-RMSNorm into AITER FlyDSL INT4 QuickReduce

files.patch:
@@ -86,9 +86,119 @@ def _make_quick_allreduce_for_test(
     quick_reduce.qr_quantization_min_size = quantization_min_size
     quick_reduce.use_fp16_kernels = False
     quick_reduce.world_size = 2
+    quick_reduce._flydsl_int4 = None
     return quick_reduce
 
 
+class _FakeFlyDSLInt4:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.allreduce_calls = []
+        self.closed = False
+
+    def allreduce(self, inp, out):
+        self.allreduce_calls.append((inp, out))
+        out.copy_(inp)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def supports_rmsnorm(hidden, nbytes):
+        return hidden in (2048, 4096, 8192, 16384) and nbytes < 1 << 31
+
+    def allreduce_rmsnorm(
+        self, inp, residual, weight, eps, out, residual_out, *, gemma_norm
+    ):
+        self.allreduce_calls.append((inp, out, residual, weight, eps, gemma_norm))
+        residual_out.copy_(inp + residual)
+        out.copy_(residual_out)
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.closed = True
+
+
+def _make_flydsl_quick_allreduce_for_test() -> tuple[QuickAllReduce, _FakeFlyDSLInt4]:
+    quick_reduce = _make_quick_allreduce_for_test(min_size_mb=2)
+    quick_reduce._ptr = 0
+    fake = _FakeFlyDSLInt4()
+    quick_reduce._flydsl_int4 = fake
+    return quick_reduce, fake
+
+
+def test_flydsl_int4_should_quick_allreduce_gates_bf16_payloads():
+    quick_reduce, _ = _make_flydsl_quick_allreduce_for_test()
+
+    at_min = torch.empty(MB, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    assert quick_reduce.should_quick_allreduce(at_min)
+    # The HIP kernels take fp16; the FlyDSL kernel is bf16-only.
+    assert not quick_reduce.should_quick_allreduce(torch.empty(MB, dtype=torch.float16))
